newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kyrgyz mourn victims of India air disaster.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyz mourn victims of India air disaster.

text.p: Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev sent a message of condolence on Thursday to the families of 13 traders from the central Asian state who died aboard the Kazakh cargo plane involved in Tuesday's mid-air collision over India.

A foreign ministry official in the capital Bishkek told Russia's Itar-Tass news agency relatives stood little chance of compensation under international rules because Kyrgyzstan was too poor to subscribe to international airline conventions.

The 13 Kyrgyz nationals, among 27 passengers and 10 crew killed on the Kazakh Ilyushin plane, were mostly so-called "shuttle traders" -- people with small businesses who import goods to former Soviet republics after making trips abroad.
Tass did not say what was contained in Akayev's message.
The agency reported from Kazakhstan that the plane's owners, the financially troubled state airline Kazakhstan National Airways, was investigating why so many passengers were aboard.
The agency said the plane had been supposed to fly to Delhi empty and return with cargo to Bishkek.
The crash killed 349 people, 37 on the Ilyushin Il-76 and 312 on the Saudi Boeing 747 jet it collided with. The cause of the collision has not yet been established.
